questions.question: What do you need in every recursive method to avoid an infinite loop?
options: A while loop as a fallback
explanations: Recursion does not use while loops.
Correct. The base case is the condition that stops the recursion. Without it, the method calls itself indefinitely.
Static variables have nothing to do with stopping recursion.
try-catch handles exceptions; it does not control recursion.

questions.question: What are varargs (double... nums)?
options: An array that receives 0 or more arguments of the same type
explanations: It is not a simple variable.
Correct. double... nums is treated internally as a double[] containing all the arguments.
It is valid syntax since Java 5.

questions.question: What is the problem with the simple Fibonacci recursion?
options: It does not compute the numbers correctly
It recalculates the same values many times
It does not work in Java
It only works with negative numbers
explanations: Correct. fibonacci(5) calls fibonacci(4) and fibonacci(3), which in turn call others, recalculating the same values multiple times.
Negative numbers are handled by the base case.
